title: Built by hand, with a partner
summary: How Christian built everything at christiangehrke.com with AI as a partner rather than a replacement: ProPre and the coloring book prompts, the lake, the Studio and the narrators, the house rules that keep every fact his own and every picture labeled real or AI, and why it still feels handmade.
fieldNotes: Drafted by Claude for Christian (Oct 19, 2026) at his request: "a note about the role of AI and how I've used it to build everything at my name domain, in a way that still has a handmade feel but partnering strategically with AI to build a better website and not just an AI built website... You were here the whole time with me. Even with ProPre and the coloring book prompts." Every fact is from his published Notes (the case studies, ProPre, the coloring books, GlazyArray, A.L.T.A., Starlee, the hammock and Two lakes Notes) and his own words in the Studio and in our sessions (the house rules in CLAUDE.md, real vs AI labels, the motion rule from the Tumble, Starlee's name, ROLLING TERRAIN and his motto, the night the clips were rescued, Oct 18-19). Nothing in it is invented; where a fact isn't his, the draft leaves it out.

post.title: Built by hand, with a partner
post.body:
Everything at christiangehrke.com was built with AI. None of it was built by AI. That difference is the whole story, and it's why the site still feels like mine.

I've built websites since 1997. In May 2026 a side project brought me back: ProPre, a tool in the browser that takes a coloring book from its first prompt to a print-ready cover. Eight single-page prototypes came out of one day with Gemini. Within two days there was a first working version, and by June it was talking to Claude. Since then everything on this site has been built the same way: the lake, the Parts Catalog, the Workshop, the Studio, the Field Notes and the made-up magazines on the newsstand.

## Who decides

Here's how the work splits. The AI writes most of the code, drafts the words and writes prompts for pictures. I decide what the site is. The ideas are mine: A.L.T.A. came to me on October 9, the brass automaton that ties the tools together is my parable, and Starlee got her name after someone told me I could do better than Robot Marley. The taste is mine too. The rides, the drone flights and the coloring books are real, and so is every call about what stays and what goes.

GlazyArray, the narrator, is a good example. Claude wrote the prompts for her and I rendered the clips. Helena didn't like the first voice, so it changed. Her eyes took three tries: no whites, then alarming whites, then calm. None of that came from a machine having taste. It came from us looking at it and saying no, not yet.

## The house rules

What makes it a partnership and not an "AI built" site is a short list of rules every AI that works here has to follow. They're written down in the code itself, and they started as things I said out loud:

Facts on the site come only from my Notes or my own words. When a draft doesn't know something, it asks me rather than guessing. Did this ride start or end at home? Who's in the hammock? How were these pages made? People stay anonymous unless they've agreed to be named, and home is never on the map. No brands or text inside AI pictures.

Every picture says whether it's real or made with AI, and real gets labeled just as clearly as AI. I fly a drone under an FAA Part 107 certificate and have since 2018. Those photographs are real, and I want people to know which ones they are.

> We need to try and be clear about what is real as much or more than what is AI.

And nothing on the page snaps. Every light fades, every scroll eases. That one is a lesson from the Tumble, and it's the kind of thing a person notices that a model never would.

## The coloring books

The coloring books are where the partnership is most obvious and most handmade at the same time. The pages are made with AI, but the prompts behind them took months to refine, tailored to each subject, and I built my own tool to help write them. A coffee book you color while drinking coffee. Salads that pair the ingredients with the finished dish, so the book works as a cookbook. Small worlds inside jars. The catalog has 101 titles in it, and 8 are published so far.

## Why it still feels handmade

Because it's slow in the right places. Things get tried, looked at and thrown out. A magazine called COL & COBBLE became ROLLING TERRAIN because I only own a mountain bike and I like to cruise. The tagline is my own motto: I'm not here to break records, I just don't want to break anything. That's how I build the site too.

The partner is there on a Sunday afternoon when a Note full of video clips won't save, and it finds the bug, fixes the server and builds a way to get the clips back. But the Note is still mine. So is the site.

blocks.title: Step by step: how a Note gets made

items.title: I gather it
items.text: Photos, clips, a track and a voice note go into a Drive folder, or straight into the Studio.

items.title: The Studio brings it in
items.text: Videos stay on my server to be trimmed into loops, and bracketed photos are merged. I mark every picture real or made with AI.

items.title: Claude drafts, and asks
items.text: A first draft from my notes only, with a list of questions for anything it doesn't know rather than a guess.

items.title: I answer and edit
items.text: My answers go back into the Note in my words; the draft is rewritten from them.

items.title: I publish
items.text: Only I can publish. It goes live in about a minute, with its share card and a magazine to wear.

blocks.file: CLAUDE.md: the rules every AI on the site works by
blocks.code:
- Facts on the site come only from Christian's Notes or his own words.
- People stay anonymous unless they've agreed to be named.
  Never publish the home location.
- No brands, logos or text inside AI renders.
- Lights ease on and off, always. Nothing snaps.
- Never commit secrets.
blocks.note: An excerpt of the house rules, word for word. They sit at the top of the code so every AI that works on the site reads them first.

blocks.title: Glossary
blocks.text:
Prompt: the words that describe what to make, for code, a page or a picture.

Render: a picture or clip made by an image or video model from a prompt.

ProPre: my tool in the browser that takes a coloring book from first prompt to print-ready cover.

The Studio: the private back room where Notes are gathered, drafted, checked and published.

Real / Made with AI: the label every picture on the site carries, so you always know which is which.
